body.translated_text: <s>Sudhālaharī</s> (The Wave of Nectar), composed by <s>Paṇḍitarāja Śrī Jagannātha</s>.

children.text: ullāsaḥ phullapaṅkeruhapaṭalatanmattapuṣpaṃdhayānāṃ nistāraḥ śokadāvānalavikalahṛdāṃ kokasīmantinīnām /
children.translated_text: A delight for the bees intoxicated by the expanse of fully blooming lotuses, a deliverance for the <s>cakravāka</s>-wives whose hearts are distressed by the wildfire of grief,

children.text: utpātastāmasānāmupahatamahasāṃ cakṣuṣāṃ pakṣapātaḥ saṃghātaḥ ko 'pi dhāmnāmayamudayagiriprāntataḥ prādurāsīt || 1 ||
children.translated_text: a calamity for the darkness, a favor to eyes whose radiance has been impaired — some extraordinary aggregate of splendors has appeared from the edge of the Sunrise Mountain.

children.text: padmadrohoddhurāṇāṃ dhavalitaharitāmaindavīnāṃ dyutīnāṃ darpaṃ drāgdrāvayanto vidaladaruṇimodrekadedīpyamānāḥ /
children.translated_text: Quickly melting the pride of the lunar rays — those white-green beams fierce in their hostility to lotuses — blazing with the excess of redness from the rim of the [solar] disk,

children.text: dūrādevāndhakārāndhitadharaṇaitaladyotane baddhadīkṣāste dainyadhvaṃsadakṣā mudamudayadinodveladusrā diśantu || 2 ||
children.translated_text: pledged from afar to illuminating the earth's surface blinded by darkness, capable of destroying wretchedness — may they, whose ruddy hue overflows with the joy of the rising day, grant us delight.

children.text: trātāmīvārtalakṣāḥ pratidinavihitānekagīrvāṇarakṣā bhaktānāṃ kalpavṛkṣāḥ sphuradanalagatasvarṇabhāsāṃ sadṛkṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: Whose aim is to protect the afflicted, who daily provide manifold protection to the gods, wish-fulfilling trees for devotees, resembling the radiance of gold placed in blazing fire,

children.text: lokakṣemāttadīkṣā nalinapariṣadāṃ dattasaubhāgyalākṣā durvṛttadhvaṃsadakṣā mama ravikiraṇāḥ santvaghānāṃ vipakṣāḥ || 3 ||
children.translated_text: whose gaze is for the welfare of the world, who bestow the lac of good fortune upon the assembly of lotuses, capable of destroying wicked conduct — may the rays of the sun be adversaries of my sins.

children.text: prāleyānāṃ karālāḥ kavalitajagatīmaṇḍaladhvāntajālāḥ strātasvarlokapālā vidaladaruṇimakṣiptabālapravālāḥ /
children.translated_text: Terrible to the frost, [destroying] the web of darkness that has swallowed the sphere of the earth, protectors who have sheltered the celestial realms, casting forth young coral-like redness from the [sun's] disk,

children.text: viśliṣyatkokabālājvaraharaṇabhavatkīrtijālairjaṭālā vyomavyāptau viśālāstvayi dadhatu śivaṃ bhāsvato bhānumālāḥ || 4 ||
children.translated_text: matted with nets of glory born from removing the fever of the separated young <s>cakravāka</s> birds, vast in pervading the sky — may the garlands of rays of the radiant <s>Bhāsvat</s> (the Sun) bestow blessings upon you.

children.text: nirbhidye kṣmāruhāṇāmatighanamudaraṃ yeṣu gotrāṃ gateṣu drādhiṣṭhasvarṇadaṇḍabhramabhṛtamanasaḥ saṃnidhitsanti pādān /
children.translated_text: When the very dense interiors of the trees are pierced by those [rays] that have entered the hollows, the bees, their minds filled with the delusion that [the rays] are the firmest golden staffs, wish to settle at their feet;

children.text: yaiḥ saṃbhinne dalāgrapracalahimakaṇe dāḍimībījabuddhyā cañcūcāñcalyamañcanti ca śukaśiśavasteṃ 'śavaḥ pāntu bhānoḥ || 5 ||
children.translated_text: when the dewdrops trembling on leaf-tips are scattered by them, the young parrots, thinking them pomegranate seeds, make their beaks restless — may those rays of the sun protect [you].

children.text: ahni krīḍocitānāṃ sarasiruhalasanmandirāṇāṃ prabhāte prodghāṭya drākkapāṭānyatha kumudagṛhānmudrayanto vimuktān /
children.translated_text: At dawn, quickly throwing open the doors of the lotus-abodes — those shining mansions suited for daytime play — then sealing shut the freed moonlily-houses,

children.text: siñcantaḥ kiṃ ca bhūmītalamakhilamapi kṣuṇṇakāśmīranīraiḥ pāyāsuḥ śrīsaparyāviracanapaṭavaḥ padmabandhoḥ karā naḥ || 6 ||
children.translated_text: and moreover sprinkling the entire surface of the earth with waters of crushed saffron — may the hands of the friend of lotuses (the Sun), skilled in arranging the worship of <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī), protect us.

children.text: ālepā hiṅgulānāmiva dharaṇibhujāmacchasaudhāgramauliṣvagreṣu kṣmāruhāṇāmabhinavavidalatpallavollāsalīlāḥ /
children.translated_text: Like applications of vermillion upon the crystal palace-tops crowning the mountain-kings, on the treetops playing the sport of freshly bursting tender shoots,

children.text: prauḍhaprāleyapuñjopari citasvadirāṅgārabhārā ivārātpārāvārātprayānto dinakarakiraṇā maṅgalaṃ naḥ kṛṣīran || 7 ||
children.translated_text: like heaps of glowing charcoal placed upon a mound of dense snow, coming from afar across the ocean — may the rays of the sun bring us auspiciousness.

children.text: kīlālaiḥ kuṅkumānāṃ nikhilamapi jagajjālametanniṣiktaṃ muktāśconmattabhṛṅgāvidalitakamalakroḍakārāgṛhebhyaḥ /
children.translated_text: This entire net of the world is sprinkled with streams of saffron; the intoxicated bees are released from the prison-houses of closed lotus-buds;

children.text: utsṛṣṭaṃ gosahasraṃ bahalakalakalaḥ śrūyate ca dvijānāṃ bhāgyairvṛndārakāṇāṃ harihayaharitā sūyate putraratnam || 8 ||
children.translated_text: a thousand cows are set free; the tumultuous chattering of birds is heard — by the fortune of the gods, <s>Haritā</s>, wife of the green-horsed [Sun], gives birth to the jewel of a son [the Dawn].

children.text: yā sūte savabhūteṣvanudinamudaye cetanāyā vilāsānyāntī sāyaṃ nikāyaṃ jalanidhijaṭharaṃ saṃjarīharti sadyaḥ /
children.translated_text: She who gives birth daily at sunrise to the delights of consciousness in all beings, who, going in the evening toward the assemblage [of waters], instantly churns the belly of the ocean,

children.text: atyarthaṃ vardhayantī maṇigaṇasuṣamāsaṃpadaṃ ratnasānoḥ sā no bhānoḥ prabhā no nayanasaraṇito dūrato jātu yātu || 9 ||
children.translated_text: who excessively increases the wealth of beauty of the gem-clusters on the peak of jewels (<s>Meru</s>) — may that radiance of the sun never go far from the path of our eyes.

children.text: nīhārairnīrajānāṃ nibiḍatamatamorāśibhirlocanānāṃ śrautasmārtakriyāṇāmapi khalu niśayā nāśamālakṣya dūrāt /
children.translated_text: Perceiving from afar the destruction wrought by night — by the mists [covering] the lotuses, by the dense heaps of utter darkness [blinding] the eyes, and indeed of both <s>Śrauta</s> and <s>Smārta</s> rituals,

children.text: sadyaḥ sindhoḥ sakāśādadhikatarajavenāgatā vāsavāśāmāśāpāśānaśeṣānapaharatutarāṃ tīkṣṇabhānoḥ prabhā naḥ || 10 ||
children.translated_text: having arrived with supreme speed from the presence of the ocean toward the eastern quarter — may the radiance of the fierce sun swiftly remove all our bonds of despair.

children.text: śīte śokaṃ śaśāṅke kṛśatamarucitāmāśunāśaṃ niśāyāṃ dhikkāraṃ dhvāntavarge kumudapariṣadi prodgamaṃ dīnatāyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Bringing grief upon the cold moon, swift destruction upon the night of faintest light, contempt upon the host of darkness, the arising of wretchedness in the assembly of water-lilies,

children.text: pāṇḍityaṃ puṇḍarīkeṣvanudinamadhikāṃ kāntimāśāsu tanvannanvañcatyanvahaṃ dyāmuṣasi karuṇayā viśvavandyo vivasvān || 11 ||
children.translated_text: bestowing learning upon the white lotuses and ever-increasing beauty upon the directions daily — <s>Vivasvān</s> (the Sun), adored by the universe, ascends the sky at dawn each day out of compassion.

children.text: svāpaṃ svāpākulānāṃ gadamatha gadināmandhakāraṃ trilokyāḥ pāpaṃ pāpāvilānāṃ sapadi pariharannāgato vāsavāśām /
children.translated_text: The sleep of those overwhelmed by slumber, the disease of the afflicted, the darkness of the three worlds, the sin of those stained by sin — instantly removing all these upon arriving at the eastern quarter,

children.text: nityaprasthānalīlākupitakamalinīnarmanirmāṇakarmā viśvārtitrāṇadharmā gaganamaṇirasau pātu śarmāniśaṃ vaḥ || 12 ||
children.translated_text: whose task is to create the playful jest of angering the lotuses through his perpetual departure-play, whose nature is to protect the world from suffering — may that jewel of the sky protect your happiness forever.

children.text: antarnīraṃ nadīnāmanudinamudaye bimbitā ye samantādgīrvāṇādrerudañcanmaṇigaṇajaṭilāṃ medinīṃ darśayanti /
children.translated_text: They who are reflected daily at sunrise within the waters of rivers, showing all around the earth bristling with the rising clusters of gems on the mountain of the gods,

children.text: vipraprotkṣiptasaṃdhyāñjalijalakaṇikājālamākāśamadhye māṇikyavrātayanto mama mihirakarā māndyamunmūlayantu || 13 ||
children.translated_text: May the rays of the sun, which appear as clusters of rubies amidst the sky within the net of water drops from the <s>sandhyā</s> (twilight) oblation tossed upward by <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, uproot my lethargy. || 13 ||

children.text: pratyagroḍhāḥ pragalbhā yuvatipariṣadaḥ proṣitaprāṇanāthā yasminnastādrimauleruparimaṇimayacchatralīlāṃ dadhāne /
children.translated_text: When he, the crest-jewel of the setting mountain, bearing the playful semblance of a jeweled parasol above,

children.text: satrāsaṃ saprasādaṃ pariṇatakaruṇaṃ locanānyutkṣipanti sthemānaṃ sa priyāṇāṃ ghaṭayatu bhagavānpadminīvallabho vaḥ || 14 ||
children.translated_text: the newly-wed, bold gatherings of young women whose beloved lords have gone abroad raise their eyes with fear and with grace, with ripened compassion—may that blessed Lord, the beloved of <s>Padminī</s> (Lakṣmī), grant steadfastness to your dear ones. || 14 ||

children.text: antardyāvāpṛthivyoradhirajani bhṛtānandhakārānudārānvidrāvya drāktadīyairiva jayadaruṇaṃ śoṇitairyadvidhate /
children.translated_text: Within the space between heaven and earth, during the night, having driven away the dense darkness sustained therein, as if with its own victorious red blood, that which accomplishes [this deed],

children.text: sāyaṃ prātaśca saṃdhyāñjalimavanisurāḥ saṃprayacchanti yasmai tasmai kasmaicidetanmama paramahaṃse devatāyai namo 'stu || 15 ||
children.translated_text: to whom the earth-dwelling <s>brāhmaṇas</s> offer the <s>sandhyā</s> oblation with cupped hands at evening and morning—to that supreme <s>paramahaṃsa</s> deity, whichever it may be, let this be my salutation. || 15 ||

children.text: trāṇaṃ traiviṣṭapānāṃ taraṇamatha payastomatāmyattanūnāṃ nadyantānāmatarkyaṃ triguṇamayatayā yattrayāṇāṃ turīyam /
children.translated_text: The protection of the celestials, the crossing of those whose bodies are weakened by the flooding waters, the unfathomable [nature] of rivers, the fourth beyond the three-<s>guṇa</s> constitution of the triad,

children.text: tattādṛktundilāyāstaruṇataratamaḥsaṃtaterantakṛttvāṃ tejastrailokyatāmrīkaraṇacaturima trāyatāṃ tīkṣṇabhānoḥ || 16 ||
children.translated_text: that radiance of the fiercely blazing sun (<s>tīkṣṇabhānu</s>), which destroys the continuity of utter darkness so swollen, skilled in making all three worlds copper-hued—may it protect [you]. || 16 ||

children.text: gīrvāṇagrāmaṇībhirgaganatalagatairgīrbhirudgīthagābhirgandharvaiścāpi gītā guṇagaṇagāramodgārigāthāsahasraiḥ /
children.translated_text: Praised by the chiefs of the gods who have ascended to the sky with their hymns of <s>udgītha</s> chanting, and also by the <s>gandharvas</s> with thousands of songs that exude the fragrance of enumerated virtues,

children.text: gāhaṃ gāhaṃ gṛhālīragatikagadināṃ gandhayanto gadārtiṃ glānigrāmaṃ grasantāṃ graharuciguravo gopatergovilāsāḥ || 17 ||
children.translated_text: plunging again and again, perfuming the disease-affliction of those afflicted with immovable illness, swallowing the multitude of weariness—may the splendors of the Lord of cows (<s>Gopati</s>, the Sun), weighty as planets' radiance, [protect you]. || 17 ||

children.text: jīvāturjāḍyajālādhikajanitarujāṃ taptajāmbūnadābhaṃ jaṅghālaṃ jāṅghikānāṃ jaladhijaṭharato jṛmbhamāṇaṃ jagatyām /
children.translated_text: Shining like heated gold, resembling vitality for those whose ailments are intensified by a web of torpor, swift as a runner for travelers, rising and expanding over the world from the belly of the ocean,

children.text: jīvādhānaṃ janānāṃ janakamatha ruco jīvajaivātṛkāderjyotirjājvalyamānaṃ jalajahitakṛto jāyatāṃ vo jayāya || 18 ||
children.translated_text: the life-sustainer of people, the progenitor of radiance from the line of <s>Jīva</s> and <s>Jaivātṛka</s>—may the blazing light of the friend of lotuses (<s>jalajahitakṛt</s>, the Sun) arise for your victory. || 18 ||

children.text: prātarnirgatya gobhiḥ saha ruciviṣaye saṃcarantyo 'hni tābhiḥ sākaṃ sāyaṃ nikāyaṃ prati punarapi yāḥ saṃprayātuṃ tvarante /
children.translated_text: Going forth at dawn together with the cows and wandering with them during the day in the realm of beauty, and again at evening hastening to return together with them to their abode,

children.text: yāsāṃ divyaprabhāvastrijagadaghavanaśreṇidāhaikadāvaḥ kṣemaṃ tanvantu tā vaḥ śivamayavapuṣo vāsareśasya gāvaḥ || 19 ||
children.translated_text: whose divine power is the singular forest-fire for burning the rows of sin-forests of the three worlds—may those rays of the Lord of days (<s>vāsareśa</s>, the Sun), whose form is auspicious (<s>śivamaya</s>), bestow welfare upon you. || 19 ||

children.text: vṛndairvṛndārakāṇāṃ danutanujanuṣāṃ rakṣasāṃ ca kṣapānte gandharvāṇāṃ dhurīṇaiḥ praṇatamahivaraiḥ kiṃnarairyannaraiśca /
children.translated_text: By hosts of gods, by the offspring of <s>Danu</s> (demons), by <s>rakṣasas</s> at the end of night, by the foremost <s>gandharvas</s>, by <s>kinnaras</s> bowing with great serpents, and by men,

children.text: vidyāṃ hṛdyāṃ nijebhyo vitaradavirataṃ dīptibhirdīpayaddyāmadyādādyāmavidyāmidamudayagirerudyadarkasya bimbam || 20 ||
children.translated_text: may this orb of the rising sun from the eastern mountain, continuously distributing delightful knowledge to its own [devotees], illuminating the sky with its splendors, destroy today the primal ignorance. || 20 ||

children.text: ā pāthojāsanāyuḥ kṣaṇalavaghaṭikādyātmakaṃ kālacakraṃ prāhuḥ pūrve purāṇāgamaviṣayavido yasya līlāvilāsam /
children.translated_text: The ancients, knowers of the subjects of <s>Purāṇas</s> and <s>Āgamas</s>, declare that the wheel of time (<s>kālacakra</s>), consisting of moments, instants, and <s>ghaṭikās</s>, extending to the lifetime of <s>Brahmā</s> seated on the lotus, is but his playful sport.

children.text: bhāvānāṃ ṣaḍvikārānatha khalu gatibhiryaśca nityaṃ prasūte sa prātaḥ pauruhūte parilasati harinmaṇḍale caṇḍabhānuḥ || 21 ||
children.translated_text: And he who eternally produces the six transformations of beings through their movements—that fierce-rayed <s>Caṇḍabhānu</s> (the Sun) shines forth at the morning <s>pauruhūta</s> (Indra's) time in the emerald disc. || 21 ||

children.text: aṅgāni brāhmaṇānāmuṣasi himabharāsaṅgato bhaṅgurāṇi vyālakṣya drākprapātā ripujanitaruṣevāruṇā vāsavāśām /
children.translated_text: Perceiving quickly that the limbs of the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> at dawn are stiffened by the burden of frost, turning red with fury like an enemy's rage rushing to the eastern quarter of <s>Indra</s>,

children.text: dharmadhvaṃsoddhurāṇāmakhilamapi kulaṃ jakṣataḥ śobhitakṣmā yakṣmāṇaṃ me harantu tvaritamaghabhido bhānavaścaṇḍabhānoḥ || 22 ||
children.translated_text: may the rays of the fierce-rayed <s>Caṇḍabhānu</s> (the Sun), destroyer of sin, who devours entirely the clan of those arrogant in destroying <s>dharma</s>, adorning the earth, swiftly remove my disease. || 22 ||

children.text: viśrāntiṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ sukhamatiśayitaṃ kāmināṃ sthāyilīlāmambhojānāṃ prabodhaṃ kumudapariṣadāṃ yaścikīrṣandayārdraḥ /
children.translated_text: He who, moist with compassion, desires to bring rest to <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, surpassing happiness, the enduring play of lovers, the awakening of lotuses, and [the closing of] the assembly of night-lilies (<s>kumuda</s>),

children.text: niryātyantaḥsamudraṃ sakalamapi nṛṇāṃ bhāramādhāya vahnāvahnāyāhnāmadhīśaḥ sa bhavatu bhavatāṃ bhūyase maṅgalāya || 23 ||
children.translated_text: emerges from within the ocean, placing the entire burden of men upon fire—may he, the lord of days, be for your abundant auspiciousness. || 23 ||

children.text: drāgāhatya prabhāte rajanihimavataḥ kaumudīḥ kautukena prodyatprauḍhānukampāḥ punarapi khalu ye sāyamujjīvayanti /
children.translated_text: Those [rays] which at dawn swiftly strike with delight the moonbeams of the night laden with frost, and which in the evening again revive them with surging, mature compassion,

children.text: āruṇye pallavānāmatha gurucaraṇāḥ śakragopāvalīnāṃ te yuṣmadbhāvalīnāṃ dinakarakiraṇāḥ klāntimunmūlayantu || 24 ||
children.translated_text: and [which cause] redness in the sprouts and [in] the rows of <s>Indragopa</s> insects—may those rays of the sun, touching the feet of the great ones, uproot the weariness of those devoted to you. || 24 ||

children.text: drāgadvaitaṃ vitanvaṃstribhuvanamabhitaḥ kauṅkumīnāṃ dyutīnāṃ nyakkurvanmāndyamudrāmatha rajanirujāṃ kokasīmantinīnām /
children.translated_text: Swiftly spreading non-duality throughout the three worlds with saffron-colored splendors, suppressing the seal of lethargy and the night-born ailments of the <s>cakravāka</s> birds' wives,

children.text: tandrāndhānāndhyasindhoriha vitatatarairuddadhānaṃ karāgraiḥ svāntadhvāntaṃ dhunītāmudayagiriśiraścumbi mārtaṇḍabimbam || 25 ||
children.translated_text: May the solar disc of <s>Mārtaṇḍa</s>, which kisses the peak of the eastern mountain, which with its widely extended ray-tips draws forth [beings] from the ocean of blindness born of lethargy — may it shake off the darkness within our hearts.

children.text: śuddhaṃ brahmālavālaṃ prakṛtiśabalitaṃ yasya mūlaṃ karāstaddrādhiṣṭasvarṇaśākhā vikasadaruṇimā pallavānāṃ vilāsaḥ /
children.translated_text: Whose basin is pure <s>Brahman</s>, whose root is variegated by <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), whose branches are rays established in gold, whose charm is the blossoming redness of tender shoots,

children.text: nīlaṃ vyomālimālā surasaphalabharo dharmakāmārthamokṣāḥ sa śrīmānvāñchitārthaṃ vitaratu satataṃ sūryakalpadrumo vaḥ || 26 ||
children.translated_text: Whose garland-row is the blue sky, whose burden of divine fruit consists of <s>dharma</s>, <s>kāma</s>, <s>artha</s>, and <s>mokṣa</s> — may that glorious sun-wish-fulfilling-tree (<s>sūrya-kalpadruma</s>) constantly bestow upon you the desired objects.

children.text: nīhāraṃ nimnagābhyo nikhilanayanato nīrajebhyaśca nidrāṃ nīḍebhyo nīḍajānāṃ nikaramuṣasi ye nityamudvāsayanti /
children.translated_text: Those [rays] which at dawn always dispel mist from the rivers, sleep from all eyes and from the lotuses, and flocks of nest-born [birds] from their nests,

children.text: sāyaṃ teṣveva teṣāṃ punarapi ghṛṇayā kalpayante ca vāsaṃ te vaḥ santu prayāsaṃ ghṛṇighanaghṛṇayo hantumābaddhakakṣāḥ || 27 ||
children.translated_text: And in the evening, out of compassion, again provide shelter for those very [beings] in those very [places] — may those [rays], with their dense and radiant compassion, having girded themselves, be ready to destroy your afflictions.

children.text: saṃhṛtya drāgbahiḥsthaṃ timirakulamathābhyantaraṃ hartukāmā randhrālībhirgṛhāṇāmudaramanudinaṃ ye viśaṅkaṃ viśanti /
children.translated_text: Having quickly gathered the host of darkness standing outside, and desiring to remove [that which is] within, those [rays] which every day fearlessly enter the belly of houses through rows of apertures,

children.text: bhānoste 'mī hṛṣīkāṇyakhilatanubhṛtāṃ harṣayanto hitehā hṛdrogaṃ saṃharantāṃ himamahimahṛto hemahṛdyāḥ karā naḥ || 28 ||
children.translated_text: These sense-organs of <s>Bhānu</s> (the sun), delighting all embodied beings, seeking their welfare, golden and pleasing — may these rays, which rob the glory of frost, destroy the disease of our hearts.

children.text: brahmāṇḍaṃ maṇḍayanto viyati valayino maṇḍalairaṇḍajānāṃ pākhaṇḍāndaṇḍayanto danutanujanuṣāṃ śobhitākhaṇḍālāśāḥ /
children.translated_text: Adorning the cosmic egg (<s>brahmāṇḍa</s>), encircling the sky with the orbits of the egg-born [birds], punishing heretics (<s>pākhaṇḍa</s>), beautifying the unbroken directions of <s>Indra</s> (<s>Akhaṇḍala</s>) through the splendor of the demon-born,

children.text: ye khaṇḍānpauṇḍarīkānvidalayitumathoddaṇḍapāṇḍityabhājaste caṇḍāṃśoracaṇḍāstvaritamiha karāḥ pāṇḍutāṃ khaṇḍayantu || 29 ||
children.translated_text: Those [rays] which possess outstanding skill to split the white lotus buds — may those gentle rays of the fierce-rayed one (<s>Caṇḍāṃśu</s>) swiftly destroy your pallor.

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ pāpāvalibhyaḥ sthita iti jagade yasya vedairudākhyā ninyuḥ ke 'pyāsanārthaṃ khalu sahacaratāṃ netrayoḥ puṇḍarīkam /
children.translated_text: He whom the <s>Vedas</s> proclaim as 'standing above the rows of sins' — some brought the lotus for his seat, indeed for the companionship of his eyes,

children.text: oṣṭhāvṛksāma yasya drutakanakanibhaśmaśrukeśākhilāṅgaḥ so 'yaṃ sarvāntarātmā tava diśatutarāṃ vāsareśaḥ śivāni || 30 ||
children.translated_text: Whose lips are the <s>Ṛk</s> and <s>Sāman</s> [Vedas], whose beard, hair, and entire body resemble molten gold — may he, this inner self of all, the lord of the day, swiftly grant you auspiciousness.

body.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Sudhālaharī</s> (Wave of Nectar) composed by the illustrious <s>Paṇḍitarāja Śrī Jagannātha</s>.
